issue.title: Bug: [FRR][zebra] RSS remains elevated after config reload with tcmalloc enabled

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

On SONiC branch 202605, using FRR 10.5.4 built with --enable-gperf-tcmalloc, a configuration reload restarts BGP and creates a new zebra process.
In an affected run, zebra used approximately 57.3 MiB RSS before the reload. The replacement zebra process grew to approximately 367 MiB RSS and was still using 376092 KiB more than nine minutes after startup.
At that point, show memory zebra reported 329 MiB in “Free ordinary blocks,” while show event cpu showed that tcmalloc_timer had been invoked 50 times. The behavior is intermittent.

These memory values are specific to the `Mellanox-SN5640-C512S2` HWSKU and the `t0-isolated-d256u256s2` scale topology.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a SONiC `202605` image on the following configuration:

   - Platform: `x86_64-nvidia_sn5640-r0`
   - HWSKU: `Mellanox-SN5640-C512S2`
   - Topology: `t0-isolated-d256u256s2`

2. Confirm that FRR was built with tcmalloc:

   ```shell
   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show version"
   ```

3. Record the initial zebra PID, RSS, and allocator statistics:

   ```shell
   docker exec bgp sh -c \
     'pid=$(cat /var/run/frr/zebra.pid); ps -o pid,etimes,vsz,rss,args -p "$pid"'

   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show memory zebra"
   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show tcmalloc stats zebra"
   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show event cpu"
   ```

4. Run the sonic-mgmt authorization test on the configured testbed:

   ```shell
   pytest \
     tests/tacacs/test_authorization.py::test_fallback_to_local_authorization_with_config_reload \
     --inventory <inventory> \
     --testbed <testbed-entry> \
     --testbed_file <testbed-file>
   ```

5. Confirm that zebra has a different PID after the configuration reload.

6. Capture the following data immediately after restart and after approximately 1, 5, and 10 minutes:

   ```shell
   docker exec bgp sh -c \
     'pid=$(cat /var/run/frr/zebra.pid); ps -o pid,etimes,vsz,rss,args -p "$pid"'

   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show memory zebra"
   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show tcmalloc stats zebra"
   docker exec bgp vtysh -c "show event cpu"

   docker exec bgp sh -c \
     'pid=$(cat /var/run/frr/zebra.pid); grep -E "^(Rss|Private_Dirty|AnonHugePages):" /proc/$pid/smaps_rollup'
   ```

7. Repeat the test if necessary because the behavior is intermittent.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

For `Mellanox-SN5640-C512S2` with the `t0-isolated-d256u256s2` topology:

- Zebra RSS before reload was approximately 57.3 MiB.
- The replacement zebra process reached approximately 367 MiB RSS.
- RSS remained at 376092 KiB more than nine minutes after startup.
- `show memory zebra` reported 329 MiB in “Free ordinary blocks.”
- `tcmalloc_timer` was invoked 50 times.

Invocation of the timer callback does not prove that the allocator’s release operation was executed or that pages were successfully returned to the operating system.

After the replacement zebra finishes rebuilding state for the same HWSKU and topology, its memory usage should converge toward a stable and repeatable steady-state level.

Unused mapped pages should be returned to the operating system according to the configured tcmalloc release policy. Repeated configuration reloads should not progressively reduce available system memory

### Relevant log output

```shell
root@sonic:/home/admin# vtysh -c "show memory zebra"
System allocator statistics:
  Total heap allocated:  386 MiB
  Holding block headers: 31 MiB
  Used small blocks:     0 bytes
  Used ordinary blocks:  25 MiB
  Free small blocks:     2224 bytes
  Free ordinary blocks:  361 MiB
  Ordinary blocks:       4243
  Small blocks:          64
  Holding blocks:        35

root@sonic:/home/admin# docker exec bgp vtysh -c 'show tcmalloc stats zebra'
Tcmalloc version 'gperftools 2.16' (2.16)
Tcmalloc mallinfo statistics:
  Total heap allocated:  1024 KiB
  Holding block headers: 0 bytes
  Used small blocks:     0 bytes
  Used ordinary blocks:  0 bytes
  Free small blocks:     8192 bytes
  Free ordinary blocks:  1016 KiB
  Ordinary blocks:       0
  Small blocks:          0
  Holding blocks:        0

generic.heap_size: 1048576
generic.total_physical_bytes: 3539008
tcmalloc.pageheap_free_bytes: 1040384

root@sonic:/home/admin# top -b -n 1 | grep "zebra"
1093737 300       20   0 1024504 404916  13464 S   0.0   1.2   1:26.17 zebra
```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

resolution.title: [FRR] Backport build fix to keep libtcmalloc in DT_NEEDED for all daemons
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/29443.

SONiC sets `ENABLE_FRR_TCMALLOC = y`, and zebra still runs on glibc malloc. gcc on Debian uses `--as-needed`, which keeps a `DT_NEEDED` entry only when the binary's own objects use a symbol from that library. FRR daemons allocate through `lib/`'s `XMALLOC` macros, so the malloc calls sit in `libfrr.so.0` and the linker drops `libtcmalloc` from most daemons, zebra included.

Upstream FRR issue: https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/issues/23338

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Add SONiC FRR patch `0118`, a backport of upstream [FRRouting/frr PR 23359](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/23359). It wraps both tcmalloc libraries in `configure.ac`, so `--as-needed` keeps them:

```diff
-LIBS="$LIBS -ltcmalloc_minimal"
+LIBS="$LIBS -Wl,--push-state,--no-as-needed,-ltcmalloc_minimal,--pop-state"
...
-LIBS="$LIBS -ltcmalloc"
+LIBS="$LIBS -Wl,--push-state,--no-as-needed,-ltcmalloc,--pop-state"
```

The `--push-state`/`--pop-state` group matters. libtool moves a bare `-l` past a trailing `--as-needed`. A global `--no-as-needed` would keep every unused library too. The patch header lists the forms I measured.

#### How to verify it

Check that every installed daemon lists the library:

```bash
for d in /usr/lib/frr/*; do
  [ -f "$d" ] && head -c4 "$d" | grep -q ELF || continue
  readelf -d "$d" | grep -q libtcmalloc || echo "MISSING tcmalloc: $d"
done
```

Today it prints zebra and its peers. With the patch it prints nothing: checked=22, missing=0.

**Route-scale before/after.** KVM `vms-kvm-t0`, FRR 10.5.4, same testbed both runs with only the `docker-fpm-frr` container swapped. `sharpd` installs 500,000 routes, then withdraws them. zebra RSS sampled for 15 minutes.

| Stage | BEFORE (glibc) | AFTER (tcmalloc) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Idle baseline | 25.1 MB | 59.7 MB |
| Peak @ 500k routes | 455.5 MB | 389.3 MB |
| After 15 min | **447.8 MB** | **113.3 MB** |
| Returned to the OS | **0 MB** | **269 MB** |

The release rate is ~0.9 MB/s, matching the 1 MiB/s cap that patch `0110` sets through `zebra memory release rate`.

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [x] 202605
- [ ] 202608

202605 ships FRR 10.5.4 with `ENABLE_FRR_TCMALLOC ?= y` and the same `src/sonic-frr` submodule pointer, so it has the same defect. Confirmed on the 202605 nightly, build 1215746. The commit applies unchanged, so an auto cherry-pick should work.

#### Tested branch

- [x] master
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [x] 202605
- [ ] 202608
- [ ] N/A

#### Test result

master: build 1216687 as the BEFORE arm. Route-scale before/after run on KVM `vms-kvm-t0`, table above. zebra RSS settles at 113.3 MB against 447.8 MB held.

202605: build 1215746 as the BEFORE arm, where zebra has no `libtcmalloc` in `DT_NEEDED`. A rebuild with this patch links all 22 daemons: checked=22, missing=0. zebra `DT_NEEDED` becomes `libtcmalloc.so.4 libfrr.so.0 libjson-c.so.5 libgcc_s.so.1 libc.so.6`.

#### Description for the changelog

[frr] Keep libtcmalloc in DT_NEEDED for every daemon so zebra uses tcmalloc.

N/A — build-time link flags only.
